title: Controllers that answer with a status
summary: Map a GET route, validate the path id, and choose the response status explicitly.

scenario.briefing: Clients receive 200 with an empty body when a product id does not exist, and negative ids still reach the database. Make the route reject non-positive ids and answer 404 for a missing product.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The controller already injects ProductService, so keep that constructor.
Add @Validated on the class and @Positive on the path variable.
Change the return type to ResponseEntity<Product>.
Map the optional with ResponseEntity::ok and use orElseGet for notFound().build().

misconceptions.testDescription: A found product returns 200 and a missing product returns 404.
misconceptions.feedback: A null body still produces 200. Return ResponseEntity.notFound().build() when the optional is empty.

misconceptions.testDescription: The GET route binds a validated positive id.
misconceptions.feedback: Annotate the controller with @Validated so Spring validates method arguments before the body runs.

misconceptions.description: Returning the persistence entity as the API contract.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Choosing the statement that the entity keeps the API stable.
misconceptions.feedback: The entity follows the table. A response model keeps the API stable and hides internal columns.

sections.title: Annotations map requests
sections.body: A controller method is bound to a route by annotations. @RestController marks the class so return values are written to the response body, and @GetMapping maps GET requests to a path. The template segment {id} names a value that @PathVariable binds to a parameter.

sections.title: The response is a decision
sections.body: A handler can return the product alone, but then every outcome looks like 200. ResponseEntity wraps the body with a status and headers. Returning ResponseEntity.ok(product) for a match and ResponseEntity.notFound().build() for an empty optional makes the outcome visible to the client.

sections.title: Validate before the lookup
sections.body: Spring validates method arguments when the controller is annotated with @Validated. A constraint such as @Positive on the path variable rejects zero and negative ids with 400 before the service runs. Validation at the boundary keeps invalid identifiers out of the data layer.

A response wrapper that carries status, headers, and body.

steps.title: Controller semantics

statements.label: @RestController serializes return values into the response body.
ResponseEntity carries the status code and headers as well as the body.
Method validation for @Positive path variables requires @Validated on the controller.
Returning null from a handler automatically produces a 404 response.
Returning the entity directly keeps the API stable when the table changes.

steps.explanation: Annotations bind the method to a route, ResponseEntity makes the status explicit, and @Validated lets the constraint reject an invalid id before the lookup. A null body still produces 200 unless the handler returns a status.
hints: Compare each statement with the controller you just wrote.
A null body is written with the current status; it does not select 404.
Constraints on method arguments run only when method validation is enabled.
The entity mirrors the table; the API contract is a separate type.
